question: I work full time and want to go back for a business degree. What are the required courses for the Business Administration major, and how many credits is the major in total?
answer:
The catalog lists no bachelor's major in Business Administration; it lists the Business Administration MBA (Master of Business Administration). It also lists Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA as bachelor's majors. [14]

For the MBA:
- The 30-credit Advanced Standing Program requires 7 core courses and 3 electives. Core courses: MBAD 601 Accounting for Managerial Decision Making; MBAD 610 Becoming a 21st Century Leader; MBAD 620 Financial Management I; MBAD 638 Info Tech for Managers; MBAD 640 Marketing Management & Strategy; MBAD 660 Operations Management; MBAD 675 MBA IFK Assessment; MBAD 680 Managing Responsible Global Business. Choose 3 electives (9 credits) from the catalog's elective list. [1]
- The 42-credit Program adds 6 foundational courses (2 credits each): ACCT 510 Foundations of Accounting; BADM 510 Foundation Stats for Business; ECON 510 Foundations of Economics; FINC 510 Foundations of Finance; MGMT 510 Foundations of Management; MKTG 510 Foundations of Marketing. It also requires the 30 credits of core courses and electives above. Students in the 30-credit Advanced Standing Program do not need the foundational-course requirement. [1]

The catalog's elective list is lengthy; see https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD for all options. [1] For the MBA's total credits, the catalog says 30 credits for Advanced Standing or 42 credits for the other program. [1] Undergraduate major requirements are 40–64 credits, but that rule applies to undergraduate students, not this MBA. [2]

Contact the Anisfield School of Business at asb@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7379, (201) 684-7380, or (201) 684-7378. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MBA-MBAD) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Does Ramapo have a nursing program for adults who already have a bachelor's in another field, like an accelerated BSN?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers a Nursing Accelerated BSN (ABSN), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, for prospective students with a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally accredited institution. It is a full-time, daytime, in-person program. [1] ABSN applicants must have a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above. [10]

Admissions provides the requirements at https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/ and application instructions at https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/. [4]

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300. [4]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/)

question: What does ACCT 221 cover? Also does it count toward any gen ed category or only the business major
answer:
ACCT 221 (Principles of Financial Accounting) is a 4-credit course: “An introduction to fundamental accounting terminology, techniques, and concepts. Emphasis will be given to the recording process and analysis of financial statement construction.” No prerequisites are published. [2]

question: How many gen ed credits does a bachelors at Ramapo require in total, and what are the categories I have to cover?
answer:
The pages do not give a fixed total number of Gen Ed credits. They say the curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits” [7]. Ramapo students take ten Gen Ed courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [10].

The four keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Take Critical Reading & Writing 102 within your first 64 credits [10]. The four keystone categories are Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; Quantitative Reasoning must also be completed within the first 64 credits [10].

Choose two of these distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Values and Ethics, and the third category. The pages differ on its name: “Systems, Sustainability, & Society” [9, 10] versus “Social Systems and Society” [11]. Section 10 says at least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than your major’s school; the Fall 2026 page says the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools [10, 11].

For clarification, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [6].

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: If I start the Information Technology major as a first-year, what should I take in my first two semesters?
answer:
The catalog lists the bachelor’s major as Information Technology Management BS [14]. Its recommended graduation plan applies to students admitted during the 2026–2027 academic year [1].

- First-year fall semester (16 credits): INTD 101 – FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4); CRWT 102 – CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4); General Education Requirement * (4); and one of MATH 108 – ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS, MATH 110 – PRECALCULUS, or MATH 121 – CALCULUS I (4). MATH 108 is highly recommended [1]. First-Year Seminar is required in the fall of your first year [3].
- First-year spring semester (16 credits): two General Education Requirements * (4 each); ECON 102 – INTRODUCTION TO MACROECONOMICS (4); INFO 224 – PRINCIPLES OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY* (4); and PATH 001 – CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1 [1].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BS-INFM) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: Can you check my transcript from county college and tell me which of my credits will transfer into the business major?
answer:
I can’t check your personal transcript or determine which of your credits will transfer. Ramapo says transfer students’ transcripts are reviewed by Admissions, and specific application of accepted credits to course requirements must be approved through transfer evaluation and advisement [10].

For New Jersey community-college credits, use www.NJTransfer.org for course equivalencies and academic planning [2][5]. If you have an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college, Ramapo accepts the full degree up to the two-year-school maximum of 65 transfer credits; A.A.S. degrees and credits without an associate degree are evaluated course by course [2].

After acceptance, you receive a Transfer Credit Worksheet showing accepted credits. Coursework needing review may be submitted to the major Convener or reviewed at orientation for detailed course equivalency [4]. Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300, McBride House [2].

The catalog lists International Business BA as the bachelor's business major [12]. Its published requirements list courses, but no total credit count [1].

question: Does a statistics course like MATH 108 satisfy the quantitative reasoning gen ed, and is it required for the business admin major?
answer:
Yes. MATH 108 carries the Gen Ed attribute “Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR)” [4]. It is one of the catalog courses with that attribute; the catalog also lists MATH 100T, 101, 104, 106, and 110 [17]. Quantitative Reasoning is a required General Education category, which must be completed within the first 64 credits [6].

The catalog lists no bachelor’s major called “business admin”; it lists Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA as bachelor’s majors named for part of it, and Business Administration MBA [17]. MATH 108 is not listed in the Business Administration MBA requirements [1]. So the catalog does not establish that MATH 108 is required for a “business admin” major. The course is 4 credits and has stated prerequisites [4].

question: Honestly which would be a better fit for me as a 34 yr old working adult, nursing or computing? I'm worried about the clinical hours
answer:
I can’t determine which is a better personal fit, and the pages don’t give clinical-hour schedules or computing-program details. The ABSN is described as a “full-time, daytime, in-person intensive experience.” [1] The generic BSN has two years of general education and science requirements, followed by a two-year nursing sequence. [2] Neither description specifies clinical hours. The pages therefore don’t establish whether either schedule fits around your work. [1][2]

To explore your choice, Ramapo’s Cahill Career Development Center offers FOCUS 2 to help students select a major; use access code “ramapo430.” [10] You can also visit a Career Advisor for assessment information. [11] The Center for Student Success recommends gathering information, using career-center assessments, and talking with faculty in majors you’re considering. [13]

For clinical scheduling details, contact the Nursing Programs Office at (201) 684-7749. For career guidance, contact the Cahill Career Development Center at careercenter@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7444. [10][11]
